'''Burton Edgar Freeman''' (July 3, 1924 – October 4, 2016) was an American [[physicist]] and [[explosive engineer]] who researched the calculated expedition timetables for the American [[Project Orion (nuclear propulsion)|Project Orion]] [[nuclear propulsion]] spacecraft in the 1950s and 60s.<ref>{{cite book|last=Dyson|first=G.|title=Project Orion: The True Story of the Atomic Spaceship|publisher=Henry Holt and Company|year=2003|isbn=978-0-8050-7284-6|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=r_Gu4f0QxrkC&pg=PA52|access-date=2015-11-16}}</ref> He calculated timetables for round trips to Mars and Venus.

==Early Life and Education==
He was born in [[Pasadena, California]] on July 31th, 1924, the only child of Edgar Keep and Lelia Grace Freeman, and grew up in [[San Dimas, California]]. He served as an officer for the V-12 U.S. Navy College Training Program during World War II.  He then embarked upon an educational path that included graduation from [[Caltech]] in 1945 with a B.S. in  physics, followed by a M.S. from [[UCLA]], culminating with a Ph.D. in [[theoretical physics]] from [[Yale University]] in 1950. 

Freeman had married high school classmate Elizabeth (Betty) Louise Forrest in 1946.  Immediately after graduation from Yale the couple and their two children moved to [[Los Alamos, New Mexico]], where he worked at [[Los Alamos Scientific Laboratory]] as a [[nuclear physicist]].  

==Project Orion and Later Work==
In 1958 the Freeman family, now with four children, returned to California. He joined [[General Atomics]] in [[La Jolla, California|La Jolla]], working to design and develop a nuclear powered spaceship with the Project Orion team.  He later commented that ''"In retrospect Orion was a really crazy idea. A great deal of force of personality and intellect drove this project".'' 

In 1967 he became a principal founder of Systems, Science and Software (S-Cubed), an advanced scientific research facility in [[San Diego, California|San Diego]].  He then served as a principal scientist at [[Science Applications International]], then at Physical Dynamics Inc., and at [[Maxwell Technologies]].  His forte was envisioning and building complex, computer-based mathematical models of complicated physical processes (e.g., [[atmospheric physics]]).<ref>https://www.alumni.caltech.edu/burton-e-freeman/</ref>

==Personal Life and Retirement==
Outside of work, Burt was an avid tennis player into his mid-80’s.  He was an avid gardener and landscaped the grounds of two homes in La Jolla. After he retired, he undertook volunteer work, evaluating the ideas of local water districts and sharing a scientific viewpoint about them that could affect their plans and decisions. 

Betty died in May 2013. Freeman remained in San Diego until 2015, when he moved to [[Kihei, Hawaii]] and remained there until his death on October 4, 2016. He was survived by six of his seven children, and five grandchildren.<ref>https://www.sandiegouniontribune.com/obituaries/burton-edgar-freeman-kihei-ca/</ref>
